title: The Virgin Birth
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: The virgin birth means that Jesus Christ was conceived by the Holy Spirit and born of the virgin Mary. His coming was God’s work, showing that salvation begins with divine grace, promise, and power.
summary: The virgin birth means that Jesus Christ was conceived by the Holy Spirit and born of the virgin Mary. His coming was God’s work, showing that salvation begins with divine grace, promise, and power.
christFocus: Jesus is the promised Son whose birth was unlike any other because He is both truly human and truly divine. The virgin birth points to His unique identity and saving mission.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
The birth of Jesus was not ordinary. Mary conceived by the Holy Spirit before she and Joseph came together. The child born to her was truly human, yet His conception was the miraculous work of God.

The virgin birth shows that salvation is not produced by human strength. God acted according to His promise and power to send His Son into the world at the appointed time.

This doctrine also points to the uniqueness of Christ. He is born of woman, under the law, to redeem those under the law. He truly enters humanity, yet He comes as the holy Son of God.

The virgin birth belongs to the larger Gospel story. The promised Immanuel has come. God is with His people in the person of Jesus Christ, who saves His people from their sins.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
If the virgin birth is treated as unnecessary or optional, the uniqueness of Christ’s coming is weakened. Scripture presents His birth as God’s miraculous act tied to His identity and mission.

This doctrine encourages faith in God’s power. The God who brought His Son into the world by His own promise and Spirit is able to accomplish salvation where human ability cannot.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Honor the birth of Christ as the gracious work of God. Do not reduce Jesus to a merely natural religious figure. Trust the promised Son who came by divine power, entered real human life, and saves His people from their sins.
